options: Tabsend settings [alt=] Settings Sending Send in one click Clicking the Tabsend icon sends the tab right away, without asking which device. Now: clicking the icon shows your devices so you can pick one. Send to You get 4 seconds to undo. Right-click the icon to pick a different device. Confirm each send An in-page toast naming the device. Errors always show. Show the waiting row in the device list “⏳ 1 waiting for …” while a send is queued to an asleep device. Right-click menus Show “Send tab / link to …” when you right-click a page or link. Keyboard shortcut Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + S does what the Tabsend icon does. A second shortcut, not set at first, always sends in one click to the “Send to” device. Rebind… Receiving Notify when a tab arrives Says which window the tab opened in; click it to go there. The toolbar badge counts new tabs either way. History Every tab your devices send each other, and whether it arrived. A tab that never arrived can be sent again from there. The newest 50 stay on this browser for offline use. Open history Don't load website images Pictures load directly from each website, so those sites can see this browser's internet address and when it asked. Turn this on if you don't want to be tracked this way. You'll see each site's first letter instead. Devices Add a device Connect another browser or your phone to this group with a link or QR code. Useful when “Send in one click” is on, since the icon then no longer shows your devices. Finish setting up Tabsend first, then come back here to add a device. Advanced details For a home-network relay, use its browser address. With the included self-signed LAN setup, that is http://<LAN-IP>:8786 ; https://<LAN-IP>:8787 is for the Android app. You can paste a relay address or a setup link. Tabsend checks whether it is the relay you are already on (then only the address changes and your devices stay paired) or a different one (then it opens setup, and keeps the current pairing until the new relay accepts this browser).
